name: American Express
title: How American Express makes money, live: fees, interest and where it goes
description: American Express's $72.2B year as a live clock: merchant discount revenue, card fees and interest, rewards and credit costs, buybacks and dividends. From the FY2025 10-K.
tagline: A card company that earns 52% of its revenue from merchants, 14% from card fees and 24% from interest.

card_stat.note: FY2025 10-K average, net of interest expense

10k: American Express Company, Form 10-K for the year ended Dec 31, 2025 (filed Feb 6, 2026)
facts: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts, American Express Co (CIK 0000004962): annual figures from each year's 10-K

blocks.label: projected from annual 10-K averages
blocks.note: Each counter = 2025 total from the 10-K ÷ 31,536,000 seconds. These are averages, not real-time. Revenue here is "total revenues net of interest expense", the 10-K's headline revenue line. [[10k]]

sections.title: Money in, money out
sections.lede: A card company earns from merchants, cardholder fees and interest, and pays for funding, credit losses, rewards and marketing. Values in US$ billions.

blocks.title: Income statement, 2025
blocks.note: US$ millions from the 10-K: 37,401 + 9,993 + 7,471 + 25,598 = 80,463 (derived) before interest expense of 8,234, leaving 72,229. Expenses: rewards 18,409 + business development 6,457 + Card Member services 6,057 + marketing 6,252 + salaries 9,016 + other 6,987 = 53,178. 72,229 − 5,256 provisions − 53,178 = 13,795 pre-tax. [[10k]]

blocks.title: Where the profit went, 2025
blocks.note: Net income 10,833; share repurchases 5,311 (statement of shareholders' equity); common dividends paid 2,271 (cash flow statement). Retained = 10,833 − 5,311 − 2,271 = 3,251 (derived; ignores $58M of preferred dividends and other equity changes). The 10-K says buybacks plus dividends were $7.6B, about 71% of net income available to common shareholders. A bank's cash flow is mostly loans and deposits, so cash flow is not shown. [[10k]]

sections.title: Where the money comes from
sections.lede: American Express reports four business segments and revenue by region. Regional figures include management allocations. It does not disclose revenue by US state.

blocks.title: Revenue by source, 2025
blocks.note: Net interest income = interest income 25.6B − interest expense 8.2B. The four lines add to 72,229, the 10-K's total revenues net of interest expense. [[10k]]

blocks.title: Revenue by region, 2025
blocks.note: Excludes −$271M unallocated. Regions are based in part on internal allocations that involve management's judgment. [[10k]]

items.title: net card fees, up 18%
items.text: Net card fees were $7.3B in 2023, $8.4B in 2024 and $10.0B in 2025. The average fee per card rose from $92 to $117 over two years, as more members move to fee-paying premium cards. The 10-K credits new Card Member acquisition and product refreshes.

items.title: of revenue goes to rewards, benefits and merchant incentives
items.text: Card Member rewards 18.4B + business development 6.5B + Card Member services 6.1B = $30.9B, or 43% of net revenue (derived). That is the biggest cost, ahead of salaries ($9.0B) and marketing ($6.3B). Card Member services rose 27% on the new US Platinum benefits.

items.title: average discount rate, falling slowly
items.text: Discount revenue was 2.24% of billed business in 2025, 2.27% in 2024 and 2.29% in 2023. Billed business grew 8% to $1,669.8B. The 10-K cites shifts in geographic and merchant spend mix.

items.title: net interest income, up 12%
items.text: Interest income $25.6B less interest expense $8.2B. Growth came from revolving loan balances, partly offset by lower rates. Customer deposits rose $13.0B in the year.

items.title: returned to shareholders
items.text: $5.3B of buybacks (16.8 million shares at an average $312.87) and $2.3B of dividends, about 71% of net income to common, per the 10-K. The quarterly dividend goes from $0.82 to $0.95 starting with the Q1 2026 declaration.

sections.title: Five years of results
sections.lede: Revenue net of interest expense and net income by year, from the 10-Ks. Buybacks here are cash paid for repurchases and other (cash flow statement), which includes shares withheld for taxes, so they differ slightly from the $5.3B of repurchases above.
